podcast.body: For this LP, Costello immersed himself fully in country music, recording in Nashville with producer Billy Sherrill, known for his work with legends like George Jones and Tammy Wynette. The album consisted entirely of country cover songs, including the lead single, Costello's rendition of George Jones's hit "A Good Year for the Roses." Despite the artistic departure, the album charted even lower than "Trust," and Costello and The Attractions found the experience of working with Sherrill unenjoyable, though it fulfilled a creative urge and allowed Costello to "hit the reset button" on his career, opening the door for future experiments. "it scratched an itch for Elvis and hit the reset button on his career, freeing him to try other experiments."
